c.tagline: The Netherlands' oldest city — riverside squares, cave-riddled hills and Burgundian flair.

taxi.fareNote: Fares follow regulated maximum tariffs and are pricey; booking by app or using a taxi rank is standard, street hailing is uncommon.

emergency.note: 112 reaches police, fire and ambulance; for non-urgent police matters call 0900-8844.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in Carnival and market crowds, and mind fast-moving bikes in cycle lanes.

hood_desc: The medieval left-bank heart around two grand squares — the café-lined Vrijthof, dominated by the Saint Servatius Basilica and Saint John's red tower, and the market square (Markt) with its town hall; here too is the fabled Bookstore Dominicanen set in a Gothic church. The walkable base for first-timers.

The characterful right-bank quarter by the station, linked to the old town by the medieval Sint Servaasbrug, with the boutique-lined Rechtstraat and buzzing restaurants and bars; best for dining, nightlife and easy train access.

A sleek modern district on the right bank, master-planned around the Bonnefanten Museum and the Céramique library, with contemporary architecture, riverside promenades and a calm feel; suits travellers wanting quiet and design.

The atmospheric old artists' and students' quarter southwest of the centre, threaded by the little Jeker river, with the medieval Helpoort gate, hidden gardens, galleries and cosy bars; bohemian and full of charm.

The green southern edge climbing toward the Sint-Pietersberg, honeycombed with the famous man-made marl caves and crowned by Fort Sint Pieter, with grand villas and the Jekerdal valley; the gateway to Limburg's hills, best for nature and calm.

water.note: Tap water is safe and of excellent quality.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless debit/credit card, phone or OV-chipkaart directly on the readers when boarding and alighting (OVpay), or buy a ticket from the driver; fares are distance-based, a single city trip runs roughly €2–3.50 (~$2.20–3.80). Regional day tickets are available.
transit.hours: City and regional buses run from about 6am to midnight; late-night service is limited, so plan evenings around the schedule or use a taxi.
transit.note: Maastricht has no metro or tram — compact and flat, it is best covered on foot or by bike, with Arriva buses filling in for longer trips.

air: Brussels, Liège & Cologne airports reachable by train
bus: Maastricht Bus Station (at Maastricht railway station)

transit.m: Arriva bus 30 to Maastricht railway station, ~25 min
Arriva bus 30 to Sittard station for onward rail

tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up the bill or leaving 5–10% for good service is normal but never expected.
